title: CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR. On creation in general; from God to His efficiencies
english: CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR. On creation in general.

Thus far we have seen concerning GOD, prince and king of man and of all things, as to His essence and subsistence, by which His sufficiency is contained, as the primary object of Christian religion — both what His nature is or what sort God is, and who He is, or why this nature is to be attributed, lest something unsuitable be attributed to the highest true God, or another or alien GOD be held for that true and highest: there follow His efficiencies, as causes on account of which religion is owed to God, namely creation and the restoration of man.

The necessity of Christ and of Christian religion hangs and shines chiefly from these two causes, on account of which God rightly demands it from men — both as creator and as savior in the Son of His love, under which is also contained that He wills to be glorifier.

title: Against curious decree-disputes; creation as alphabet of revelation
english: At length indeed and learnedly there are commonly inserted here dogmas concerning divine decrees and counsels, whose consideration, as it is hard and abstruse, so will be undertaken most well and safely of all a posteriori in their own places: lest we further divide the German churches already long enough divided by dangerous altercations concerning predestination, reprobation, providence, as some years past happened, alas, in neighboring Belgium.

But soberly and with great religion, without scrupulosity, we must think and speak concerning the Lords counsels and ways — Isaiah 55; Romans 11:33-34. Nothing here can flesh and blood, but all things are to be sought from the heavenly Fathers Apocalypse, which Genesis 1:1 God in the beginning and before all things made known through the act of CREATION of these heavens and this earth, which certainly is the revelation of revelations, and by its power embraces all the rest. This is the alphabet of every notion and action.

title: II-III: creation considered in itself; definition
english: II. But creation is to be considered both in itself and in order to creatures. III. Creation considered in itself is Gods action by which God the Father through the Son in the Holy Spirit produced from nothing heaven and earth and all things that are in them — Genesis 1:1; Psalm 33:9; Hebrews 11:3; Revelation 4:11.

Creation is production of a thing from nothing of itself and of subject, or, as they say, from negative and privative non-being. And therefore, when we speak of permission, there is something middle between doing and hindering lest someone do; but creation properly is the effective fulfilling of the decree through Gods will and power.

title: IV-VII: immediate and mediate creation
english: IV. And it is immediate or mediate. Immediate is that by which God without a creatures medium, by His single will things — as heaven and earth in the beginning, angels, the rational soul.
VI. Mediate is that by which things are produced from principles already created, God yet primarily acting — as plants, animals from earth and waters on the following days.
VII. But the existence of things mediately created hangs no less from God than of those immediately created; for God works in all things.

title: XIII-XVI: efficient, impulsive, material causes
english: XIII. Nor is creation of all things efficiently from God alone only, but also no creature can create. XIV. But the impulsive cause of creation is Gods communicative goodness, or the love by which God willed to communicate His good outwardly.

Matter properly so called did not lie beforehand for created things; for creation is from nothing. Those who invent eternal matter with Aristotle, or two principles with the Manichees, wander from the truth.

title: XVII-XX: form and final cause; inequality of things
english: XXVII. The form of creation is the divine command itself or fiat — Psalm 33:9. From which God is called FOUNTAIN. XVIII. The final cause of creation is Gods glory, and the good of creatures subordinated to Gods glory — Proverbs 16:4; Romans 11:36; Revelation 4:11.
XX. Inequality of things is not from matter but from Gods most wise ordination, that there may be order and harmony in the universe.

XXII. And these things concerning creation commonly: there will follow creatures, which are regarded either jointly or discretely. Regarded jointly they come under the name WORLD: discretely they are called the works of the beginning, of the first night, and of the six days. CHAPTER TWENTY-FIVE, On the world, follows.
